# EKUZO

> EKUZO is a youth esports coaching organization that builds transformational programs for kids through structured practice, skilled coaching, and real competition. Tagline: Every Gamer Deserves a Team.

EKUZO runs three programs: **EKUZO Camps** (1-week intensive summer camps), **EKUZO100** (a 4-week intro program for individual gamers), and **EKUZO Teams** (a semester-based school-partnered program). All programs are fully online, run by professional coaches, and center on League of Legends with additional titles coming. The organization is based in Houston, Texas and serves the United States and North America.

Founded in 2021 by Karlin "Faith" Oei — a former peak Challenger League of Legends jungler and national collegiate captain who won over $80,000 in esports scholarships. The head coach is Sebastien "ZzLegendary" DeMontigny, who previously coached at Dignitas and Evil Geniuses.

EKUZO's pedagogy treats esports the way traditional school sports treat athletic development: consistent teammates, coach-led practice, a real season, and deliberate skill-building. The emphasis is as much on social-emotional growth (teamwork, resilience, time management, digital citizenship) as on in-game mechanics.

## Programs

- [EKUZO Camps](https://ekuzo.gg/programs/ekuzo-camps): Intensive 1-week online summer esports camp. Monday–Friday, 3 hours per day, morning and afternoon slots. Ten weekly cohorts from May 18 through August 6, 2026. $199 per week. For gamers who want a focused, high-intensity introduction to team esports during school breaks.
- [EKUZO100](https://ekuzo.gg/programs/ekuzo100): 4-week intro program for individual gamers. Two 90-minute sessions per week, coach-led, ~5 player teams. $100 total. The lowest-commitment way to experience structured team practice and see what EKUZO is about.
- [EKUZO Teams](https://ekuzo.gg/programs/ekuzo-teams): Semester-based esports program structured like a school sport. 16 weeks, two 90-minute sessions per week, same teammates and same coach all season. Fall 2026 semester runs August 31 through December 18. Pricing: $576 paid in full (10% discount) or 4 × $160 monthly installments ($640 total). Best fit for gamers ready for season-long commitment, and for schools partnering with EKUZO on an official esports program.
- [All programs overview](https://ekuzo.gg/programs): Side-by-side comparison of the three programs.

- [Methodology](https://ekuzo.gg/methodology): EKUZO's full coaching philosophy, the 10 pillars of the program, how practice is structured, and what makes EKUZO different from unstructured online gaming.

- [For Schools](https://ekuzo.gg/schools): How schools partner with EKUZO to run an official esports program, including curriculum integration, coaching, and tournament organization.
- [Games](https://ekuzo.gg/games): The game titles EKUZO currently supports, with League of Legends as the primary platform.

## Blog and articles

- [Blog index](https://ekuzo.gg/blog): All EKUZO blog posts — guides for parents, family case studies, and student testimonials.
- [What your kid's gaming is telling you](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/what-your-kids-gaming-is-telling-you): Karlin Oei's parent-facing perspective piece on how to read the meaning behind a gamer kid's behavior, especially the quiet kid who plays as much as anyone but won't claim the word "gamer." Walks six common signs (the meltdown after a loss, the unfocused hours, the fight over logging off, the in-game social life that doesn't carry outside, the downplaying, the talented-but-stuck frustration) with the easy surface read against what each usually means underneath. Synthesizes that a kid's gaming is rarely about volume and is usually about a meaningful activity that lacks a container, and that the container only works when its culture is right. Closes with Karlin's own founder story of growing up gaming through social anxiety and an $80,000 esports scholarship turnaround. Cites Pew 2024, APA 2025, Columbia/JAMA 2025, and NASEF.
- [When gaming helps homeschool kids and when it hurts](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/when-gaming-helps-homeschool-kids): Karlin Oei's parent-facing guide on when gaming grows a homeschooled kid and when it shrinks their world. Argues the environment around the game — an adult nearby, a stable group, a goal, deliberate game choice, and reflection afterward — decides the outcome far more than raw hours. Includes a five-question parent gut-check, the research on addictive use versus total screen time, and Karlin's own story of esports scholarships turning around a capable kid that school nearly lost. Pillar piece, cross-linked with the companion case study.
- [What 200+ homeschool parents taught us about gaming](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/what-homeschool-parents-taught-us-about-gaming): A case-study reading of a 200+ parent homeschool thread on kids and gaming. Sorts the responses into three camps — cut it off (60%), set limits (30%), aim it (10%) — with the language each camp uses, which games worried parents (Fortnite, Roblox) and which did not (Minecraft), and the single structured, social, supervised version of gaming all three camps are really asking for. Companion case study to the homeschool gaming pillar piece.
- [Why League of Legends is perfect for youth development](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/league-of-legends-youth-development): Karlin Oei's parent-facing guide on why League of Legends works as the backbone of structured youth coaching when the format is right. Covers the toxicity question, why League beats Fortnite / Minecraft / Roblox / VALORANT for a coaching system, what the Jynxzi creator tournament showed about format shaping behavior, and how EKUZO handles solo-queue risk through stable teams and coached voice. Includes a 5-item FAQ on age-appropriateness, transferable skills, and onboarding new players.
- [Virtual summer camps for kids who'd rather be gaming (still open for summer 2026)](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/summer-camps-for-kids-who-game-2026): Parent's guide comparing the four categories of summer gaming camps (game-design and coding, creation-focused, university-and-in-person, structured esports), with representative camps, cost ranges, hours per week, and coach type per category. Includes a detailed explanation of why League of Legends suits youth structured programs and how EKUZO Camps are run.
- [Our Family's Esports Journey with EKUZO and the K1ng](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/our-family-s-esports-journey-with-ekuso-and-the-k1ng): Parent testimonial. Lisa Holt's story of how her son Ryan ("K1ngofbattle") regained confidence and developed leadership through EKUZO after being bullied in junior high.
- [Conquering my Mountain and Giants: How Esports Changed My Life](https://ekuzo.gg/blog/conquering-my-mountain-and-giants-how-esports-changed-my-life): Student testimonial. John Hay's story of working through anxiety, perfectionism, and near-failing grades with the help of an EKUZO coach.
